newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai vice squad officer finds tables turned.
newsitem.headline: Thai vice squad officer finds tables turned.

text.p: A Thai policeman assigned to help remove vice from the notorious sex and sand resort of Pattaya found the tables turned when a woman he spent the night with stole his car and gun.
Police said on Friday that a woman had been arrested on charges of stealing the car, gun, mobile phone and other valuables from Private First Class Itthiphol Warayu as he slept in a love motel.

Itthiphol, a member of a task force sent to Pattaya a week ago to crack down on vice, had met the woman on Wednesday night and went to the motel with her. He woke up in the morning to find the woman gone, along with his possessions and his car.
"The suspect said she had just driven the car around to show her friends, but Itthiphol insisted that she meant to steal from him so we had to detain her," a police officer said.

Thailand has deployed hundreds of police to Pattaya in an effort to clean up the city after Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh declared it a "dirty town" following repeated reports of widespread drug abuse and organised crime groups who prey mainly on tourists.
Pattaya police frequently receive complaints of women drugging and robbing tourists who often come to Pattaya for its sex industry.

Women have been accused of coating their nipples with tranquilisers which knock men out after they lick the drug. Others put drugs into their victims' drinks then rob them after they pass out, police said.

At least 45 foreign tourists have been found dead of heart failure in Pattaya over the past year. Police and hospital sources said the heart failure could have been caused by an overdose of the drugs used to knock the men out.
